title: Single-cell suspensions from primary human esophagus tissue
author: Annette Hayden
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t9ver66
materials: Strain with a 70 um cell strainer.
Keep on ice from this point.
Count the cells and record cell viability

steps.title: Wash Tissue
steps.instruction: Wash the primary human esophagus tissue in PBSA.

steps.title: Digest Tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the minced tissue to the Collagenase/DNAse solution in a 50ml Falcon tube and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Shake the suspension at 110-150 rpm for 60 mins at 37°C with the tube on its side to increase agitation.
At 15, 30, and 60 mins, pipette the suspension up and down thoroughly using descending sized pipettes (25, 10, and 5 ml).

steps.title: Sieve and Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Sieve the digested tissue and isolate the cells.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 ml DMEM (empty) to the sieve and push through with a syringe plunger.
Centrifuge at 1500 rpm for 5 mins and remove the media.

steps.title: Perform RBC Lysis
steps.instruction: Remove red blood cells from the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in RBC lysis buffer and incubate at 4°C for 10 mins.
Add 10 ml DMEM (empty) and pipette up and down thoroughly.

steps.title: Filter and Final Wash
steps.instruction: Filter the cells and prepare the final suspension.

substeps.instruction: Pass the suspension through a 40 um cell strainer, pushing through with a plunger.
Centrifuge at 1500 rpm for 5 mins and remove the media.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of cell suspension buffer.

steps.title: Count Cells
steps.instruction: Perform cell counting using a haemocytometer.

substeps.instruction: In a 0.5ml tube, mix 10 ul of cell solution with 10 ul of trypan blue.
Add the resultant 20 ul mix onto a disposable haemocytometer (C-Chip, FR type).
